review_lens: Evidence & Correctness. Re-derived every load-bearing claim in the three planner outputs from the repository itself (Read/Grep/git show, plus two executed probes: `doorway.mutation_check.preflight()` and a psycopg `PostgresQuery.convert` reproduction). Disconfirmed weak claims; did not rewrite plans.
verdict: REVISE — the three plans converge on a defensible shape and are strongly mutually corrective, but two blocking defects survive in all/most of them, and several Observed-tagged claims are wrong or falsified by git history.
blocking_issues: BLOCKING (all three plans) — The recommended B1 classification branch is over-broad and would invert the very defect it fixes. A's WP-B, B's WP-1(a) and C's WP-B1 all specify: a `psycopg.ProgrammingError` carrying `sqlstate is None` 'never reached the database and is a 400 rejected'. Observed by execution (psycopg 3.3.4, backend/): `PostgresQuery.convert` raises ProgrammingError with sqlstate None for THREE distinct causes — (a) `cannot adapt type 'dict' using placeholder '%s'` (the caller's fault, the B1 case), (b) `query parameter missing: x` (our SQL's fault), (c) `the query has 2 placeholders but 1 parameters were passed` (our SQL's fault). Causes (b) and (c) are internal service bugs; classifying them 400 'rejected' tells the caller they made a mistake about a bug that is not there — the exact failure server.py:472-478 and documents.py:12-14 are quoted in the bug report to prevent, running backwards. No plan constrains the branch to adaptation failures. Before Gate 3 the branch must be scoped by cause (e.g. only when the parameter value's type has no dumper), not by sqlstate alone, and must have an acceptance test asserting that a missing/mismatched placeholder still returns 500 'broke'.

BLOCKING (Planner A WP-H, and Planner B WP-4 as written) — The B4 acceptance criterion is unsatisfiable against the current schema. A's WP-H: 'as an ordinary requester, a direct select using another deal's identifier returns zero rows or is refused'. Observed at backend/db/migrations/0005_run_store.sql:288-292: `grant select, insert on cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung, cw.ruleset, cw.ruleset_member ... to cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer, cw_legal_admin` and (line 292-296) `grant select ... to cw_auditor`, with RLS enabled only on cw.run, cw.run_decision, cw.run_finding (lines 265-268). A requester CAN reach all five tables directly today, so that test fails by construction — it is not a guard, it is a package that cannot pass. Only Planner C (EV-008) caught this and correctly split B4 into a source-shape test (WP-B4a, achievable now) and a separate RLS migration (WP-B4b). Gate 3 must adopt C's split or A/B's B4 packages will stall or silently pull an unscoped schema change into a 'cheap test' package.
major_defects: Planner A — the causal story behind its headline 'NEW BLOCKING DEFECT' is falsified for one of the four rows. A assumes (its own Assumed tag) that all four stale mutation patterns 'became stale in the uncommitted Phase 2 work'. Observed: `git show HEAD:backend/doorway/server.py` does not contain the pattern `selector = {k: v[0] for k, v in parse_qs(parsed.query).items() ...`; `git log -- backend/doorway/server.py` shows add0554 'Reject malformed query escapes' refactored it into `self._query(...)` (server.py:158 in both HEAD and working tree). The doorway harness was therefore ALREADY red on committed main before any Phase 2 change. A's Unresolved question #3 ('did they go stale on committed main or only in the working tree?') is answerable from git in one command and A did not run it; Planner C did (EV-004) and got it right. This matters for package sizing: WP-A/WP-0/WP-T0 is partly a repair of committed state, not only of another session's uncommitted work.

Planner A — a materially wrong description of the harness failure mechanism, which understates the blast radius. A states 'mutation_check.py:424-427 returns verdict skip when the pattern is absent; main() puts skip into missed and returns 1'. Observed: `main()` calls `preflight()` FIRST and, if it returns anything, prints 'STALE CHECKS — nothing was run, because these prove nothing' and returns 1 without running a single mutation. That is the engine harness's behaviour A described, not the doorway's. Consequence A omits and B/C state correctly: all 36 doorway guarantees are currently unevaluated, not just the four stale ones — so any plan sentence of the form 'the suite would have caught that' is unsupported for the doorway today.

Planner A — an Unresolved question that is resolvable in one `ls`. A states 'I could not read package.json — it is absent or empty at the repository root' and leaves 'is npm run verify wired to both mutation harnesses' Unresolved, which it then uses to hold overall confidence below high. Observed: there is no root package.json, but backend/package.json exists and reads `"verify": "npm run test && npm run test:engine && npm run test:doorway && npm run test:mutation"` and `"test:mutation": "node db/test/mutation-check.mjs && python engine/mutation_check.py && python doorway/mutation_check.py"`. Planners B and C both read it. A's stated confidence discount rests on a search it did not perform.

Planners A and C — runs.py is treated as an unguarded B1 bind site and it is not. A lists 'backend/doorway/runs.py (line 111 raw bind)' in WP-C's file map; C's acceptance criterion requires 'one end-to-end test per non-Write.bind binding site (POST /agreements/execute, POST /runs)' returning 400 for a dict-valued field. Observed at runs.py:111-125: `agreement_id = body.get("agreement_id"); if not isinstance(agreement_id, str) or not agreement_id.strip(): return Answer(400, ... "kind": "rejected")`. The shape check already exists and already returns 400. Planner B is correct here and additionally identifies the real, unreported sub-case: executions.py:174 `agreement_id = str(body["agreement_id"]).strip()` launders a dict into the string "{'nested': [1, 2]}" and produces a not-found rather than a 500 — a distinct failure mode named in no report. A's WP-C is scoped partly against a defect that does not exist while B's genuine finding is in only one plan.

Planner B — a rule-vs-entry counting error that propagates into its acceptance criteria. B states 'preflight() returns 5 stale entries' and then refers throughout to '5 stale rows' / 'the 5 stale mutation rows'. Observed by execution: preflight() returns 5 STRINGS covering 4 distinct MUTATIONS rows — the row 'removing an expired session crashes if another request removed it first' generates two entries (pattern gone AND names a test that does not exist). A package sized to repair 'five rows' will look for one that isn't there; A and C's count of four is correct.
minor_defects: Line-citation errors on B5 in Planners B and C. Both cite reasons[0] at runs.py:176 and :178 and manifests.py:172 and :174. Observed by grep: runs.py:176 and runs.py:179; manifests.py:172 and manifests.py:176. Planner A's citations are correct. The count (four occurrences) is right in all three.

Planner B — unjustified scope inflation on B4. bug_report.md scopes five tables (snapshot, snapshot_member, snapshot_ladder_rung, ruleset, ruleset_member); B's WP-4 and its acceptance criterion enumerate SIX by adding cw.audit_checkpoint, which appears in the quoted pg_class output alongside cw.schema_migration but is append-only audit infrastructure the contract's hard constraint 5 fences off. B flags the five-versus-seven discrepancy in its assumptions but then silently picks six.

Planner A — a non-discriminating acceptance criterion for WP-I (B8). A requires `python -c "import doorway.sessions"` to succeed. Observed: sessions.py:28 has `from __future__ import annotations`, so the un-imported `Database` annotation at line 70 never evaluates; the import succeeds identically before and after the fix. Planner C's framing (a type checker, or removing the future import as a probe) is the only discriminating one offered.

Planner C — imprecise count on B6. C's acceptance criterion says 'every cw.audit( call site passes the event as a bound parameter ... all six sites covered'. Observed: there are three f-string statements (executions.py:323, manifests.py:240, runs.py:405) and five cw.audit( statements in non-test doorway code (adding documents.py:218 and writes.py:459, both already parameterised). 'Six' echoes the bug report's count of event-passing callers; as an acceptance criterion it is ambiguous about what must be inspected.

Planner C — overstates the mutation coupling for refusals.py. EV-005 lists the two refusals.py rows (`if code == INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGE:` and `if isinstance(error, psycopg.OperationalError):`) as at risk from B1. Verified: B1's fix inserts a branch; neither quoted line need change, so those two rows do not go stale. The manifests.py row quoting `                    "reason": reasons[0],` genuinely does break under B5 — that one is exactly right and is the strongest instance of C's point.
missed_risks: No plan constrains the new 400 branch from leaking driver text. refusals.py:107 currently returns `Refused(status=400, reason=reason, kind="rejected")` where `reason` is the raw driver/diag message; refusals.py:80-83 and :101-103 explicitly forbid driver detail reaching the caller ('the driver's message — which names hosts and ports — must not leave the building'). A sqlstate-None branch routed through that path would emit "cannot adapt type 'dict' using placeholder '%t' (format: TEXT)" to the caller. Any B1 package needs an acceptance criterion that the 400 body carries a field-naming sentence the module authored, not the driver's.

No plan specifies `current_setting('cw.actor', true)` for the A-1 minimal policy. The one-argument form raises 42704 (undefined_object) when the GUC is unset rather than evaluating false; the two-argument missing_ok form returns NULL. Since refusals.classify routes a non-DataError psycopg error to 500 'broke', a policy written with the one-argument form turns any unset-actor path on cw.session into a service-broke 500 instead of a clean refusal. This is an implementation detail the package must fix, not discover.

All three plans put session mutation-row repair in package one while sessions.py is dirty with another session's in-flight work. Observed `git status --porcelain`: `M backend/doorway/app.py`, `M backend/doorway/server.py`, `M backend/doorway/sessions.py`, `M backend/doorway/test_sessions.py`. Repairing the three session rows means quoting UNCOMMITTED sessions.py text; if the concurrent session (contract assumption A5) revises Phase 2 before committing, the repaired harness is stale again on arrival. No plan states a guard (sequence WP-0 behind the Phase 2 commit, or quote only lines the Phase 2 diff does not touch). This is the same class of failure the package exists to fix.

engine/mutation_check.py has NO preflight function, so the 'run a static preflight over both harnesses' acceptance criterion in Planners A and B requires tooling that does not exist. Verified: `engine.mutation_check` exposes only MUTATIONS and main; a stale engine pattern is only detected as SKIP after all 57 mutations have each copied the tree and run pytest, and it is fatal only at the end of a long run. I confirmed 0 of 57 engine patterns are stale by an ad-hoc script, but the engine harness cannot detect its own staleness cheaply and its rows are never checked for named-test existence — a gap none of the plans names, and one that matters precisely because B3 (whichever way it is decided) is the change most likely to break those rows.

Adding a seventh entry to ROLE_TO_DB_ROLE (A's WP-D) produces a current_user for which cw.app_role() returns NULL. Observed at 0001_foundation.sql:72-81: the CASE names only cw_viewer, cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer, cw_legal_admin, cw_auditor — it already returns NULL for cw_administrator. Planner B flags the fail-closed review requirement; Planner A proposes the map entry without it. Mitigating (and correctly noted by B): no executable test pins the map to six — I grepped; ROLE_TO_DB_ROLE appears only at db.py:65 and db.py:186 — so a seventh entry does not breach success criterion 6.
unsupported_claims: Planner A, Unresolved #2: 'package.json could not be read at the repository root, so the true blast radius of the four stale checks is inferred from bug_report.md rather than observed.' — Disconfirmed. backend/package.json is present and readable and wires verify → test:mutation → doorway/mutation_check.py.

Planner A, Assumption 1: 'The four stale mutation patterns became stale in the uncommitted Phase 2 work rather than earlier.' — Disconfirmed for the server.py row by `git show HEAD:backend/doorway/server.py` and `git log -- backend/doorway/server.py` (add0554). Confirmed only for the three sessions.py rows: `git show HEAD:backend/doorway/sessions.py | grep -c _by_token` = 10, and the named test exists at HEAD (`grep -c test_an_entry_removed_mid_check_is_no_session_not_a_crash` = 1).

Planner A, E-A2: 'mutation_check.py:424-427 ... a pattern that is not found returns skip, is appended to missed, and makes main() return 1.' — Wrong file behaviour attributed. That describes engine/mutation_check.py's main(); the doorway harness aborts in preflight() before running anything.
Planner B: 'preflight() returns 5 stale entries' rendered thereafter as five stale ROWS. — Four rows, five entries.
Planner C, EV-005 in part: the two refusals.py mutation patterns are not put at risk by B1's insertion. — Not supported; the quoted lines survive an inserted branch.
Planners A and C on runs.py as a B1 bind site. — Disconfirmed at runs.py:111-125, which already isinstance-guards and returns 400.

NOT disconfirmed, and I record it because it is the single highest-consequence claim in the set: B3's conflict with a passing test is real in all three plans. Verified verbatim at backend/engine/test_manifest.py:112-125 — test_high_is_matched_on_meaning_not_spelling asserts `checked.coerced == ()` for 'HIGH', 'high' and ' High ' with the stated rationale, and bug_report.md B3's own probe output ('kept severity: High / original claim: HIGH / coerced set: ()') is exactly the case that test pins as correct. Implementing B3 as recommended breaches success criterion 6. All three plans are right to escalate rather than code.

Also NOT disconfirmed: Planner A's A-1 bypass argument. Verified at 0013_administrator.sql:117-133 (cw.account.person is an unconstrained `text primary key`; the CHECK constraint is on `role`, not `person`), writes.py:338-348 (POST /accounts takes `person` from the body), and db.py:205 (`set_config('cw.actor', %s, true)` is fed that same person). An administrator-created account named `__signin__` with role 'viewer' would satisfy an actor-scoped policy. Planner B's counter-evidence (the role CHECK constraint) does not refute this path, because it constrains a different column.
recommended_corrections: Rewrite the B1 classification branch in whichever package owns it so it keys on the ADAPTATION failure, not on `sqlstate is None`, and add the discriminating acceptance test: a statement with a missing or miscounted placeholder must still return 500 kind 'broke', while a dict/list parameter returns 400 kind 'rejected'. Add a criterion that the 400 body does not carry the driver's sentence (refusals.py:101-103).

Adopt Planner C's B4 split verbatim: WP-B4a a source-shape test (achievable today), WP-B4b an RLS migration with its own risk budget, its own numbering decision, and regression coverage for the content-addressed sharing at runs.py:282-327 and for `security_invoker` on cw.run_snapshot / cw.run_contract / cw.run_summary. Delete A's and B's behavioural-DB acceptance criterion for B4, and settle the five-versus-six-versus-seven table count against 0005_run_store.sql rather than against the quoted pg_class output.

Correct the harness package's premise and evidence before Gate 3: four rows / five preflight entries; failure is an abort in preflight(), so all 36 doorway guarantees are currently unevaluated; and the server.py row is a repair of COMMITTED main (add0554) while the three sessions.py rows are a repair of another session's UNCOMMITTED work. Add an explicit sequencing note that the sessions.py rows cannot be written until Phase 2 is committed, or must quote only lines outside the Phase 2 diff.

Take Planner B's executions.py:174 `str(...)` laundering sub-case into the B1 package and drop runs.py from the B1 file map in Planners A and C. Verify by grep before writing the package that no other `str(body[...])` coercion exists on a bind path.

Fix the citations: reasons[0] at runs.py:176/179 and manifests.py:172/176 (A is correct, B and C are not). Replace A's WP-I acceptance criterion with C's (type checker, or remove `from __future__ import annotations` as a probe), since the import test passes before the fix.

Add to whichever package owns the A-1 policy: the policy predicate must use `current_setting('cw.actor', true)`; and, if the dedicated-role option is chosen, an explicit review that every policy calling cw.app_role() (0001_foundation.sql:72-81, which returns NULL for any current_user it does not name) fails closed under the new role.

Record in the plan that engine/mutation_check.py has no preflight, so 'zero stale on both harnesses' is not currently an executable criterion. Either scope the tiny shared preflight helper as a deliverable of the harness package, or restate the engine criterion as 'engine/mutation_check.py exits 0', which is what actually exists.

Keep, unchanged, the three areas where all three plans independently converge and my re-derivation confirms them: (i) B3 is escalated as an owner decision and not implemented (test_manifest.py:112-125); (ii) the harness repair is package one; (iii) A-1 is approval-sensitive with the dedicated-role option recommended on evidence, shipped together with the D-1 boundary test. On A-1 the tie-break should go to Planner A's bypass evidence plus Planner B's dependency list — the two are complementary, and neither plan alone sizes the package correctly.
